Plan and organize

Connect work items, Epics, and repository knowledge.

Start from a work item

Open Work items. Local items stay on your Mac; GitHub issues and Jira show remote work.

  1. Choose Local → New and add context and acceptance criteria.
  2. Start development starts the agent. GitHub and Jira items open a prepared composer first.
  3. Open the item to follow its tasks and PRs. By default it is done when its PR merges, or choose Mark finished.
  4. Push to remote… publishes it as a GitHub issue or Jira ticket.

Link work item in a Local item’s Context references other work.

Organize an Epic

An Epic groups related work items and their tasks. Any Local item, GitHub issue, or Jira ticket can be one; the grouping stays on your Mac.

  1. On workspace Home, choose Create Epic from the Epic tab, or Mark as Epic on a work item. Talk it through lets an agent draft it.
  2. Add work with Add existing or Suggest work.
  3. Track Planned, Working, and Done. Run starts a task.
  4. When a PR merges, Next in Epic suggests what to start next. Nothing starts by itself.
  5. Review the outcomes, then Conclude Epic.

Build repository memory

  1. Open Memory → Learn from my PRs, or Learn from this PR on a closed or merged PR.
  2. Check Rules, Recipes, and Specs, and edit or delete entries.
  3. Choose whether Reviews, Development tasks, or both use memory.

Memory → Check against spec has an agent compare code with a spec and reproduce failures.

Follow a Circle

Choose Circles → Create a circle, then pick people and repositories. It sends no invitations, and Insights cover only what ByteQuay has collected.

Learn with Artifacts

  1. Open Artifacts and ask in Ask about this repository. Answers cite files and end with a question card.
  2. Choose Make the page when offered, or ask for one at any time.
  3. Ask for changes in the same conversation; Versions keeps each save.

The agent reads the repository but never changes it.
